findings.problem: status is a raw String instead of a domain enum, allowing arbitrary values like "sent", "SENT", "", or any future string that does not correspond to a valid lifecycle state.
findings.failure_mode: Invalid or misspelled status strings silently enter the system; pattern matching on status is impossible; serialization may emit unexpected values that downstream consumers cannot handle.
findings.fix: Replace `pub status: String` with a `TelemetryStatus` enum (e.g., `Pending`, `Validated`, `Sent`) and use smart constructors at parse boundaries.

findings.problem: is_validated and is_sent are independent booleans that can form illegal combinations: is_validated=false and is_sent=true (sent without validation), is_validated=true and is_sent=false and sent_at_epoch_ms=Some (timestamp without being sent), both true and both false (ambiguous lifecycle).
findings.failure_mode: The compiler cannot prevent sending unvalidated telemetry; runtime checks must redundantly verify boolean combinations; logic that branches on one boolean without checking the other will silently accept invalid state.
findings.fix: Replace the three fields (status, is_validated, is_sent, sent_at_epoch_ms) with a single typestate enum that encodes the lifecycle: e.g., `enum TelemetryState { Pending { id: String } , Validated { id: String } , Sent { id: String, sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 } }`. Each variant owns its lifecycle data.

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms is a global Option<u64> on the struct rather than living inside the variant that owns it. This permits is_sent=false with sent_at_epoch_ms=Some(u64) (timestamp without send) and is_sent=true with sent_at_epoch_ms=None (sent without timestamp).
findings.failure_mode: Invalid state where telemetry appears sent but has no timestamp, or has a timestamp but was not sent. Any consumer reading sent_at_epoch_ms cannot know whether to trust it without also checking is_sent, creating invariant fragility.
findings.fix: Move sent_at_epoch_ms into the enum variant that owns the sent state, e.g., `Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 }`, so the compiler guarantees it only exists when the telemetry is actually sent.

findings.problem: id is a raw String with no domain semantics. Any String can be used as an id, including empty strings, unbounded strings, or strings that violate id format rules.
findings.failure_mode: Empty or malformed ids silently enter the system; no compile-time distinction between an id and other strings increases API misuse risk.
findings.fix: Introduce a `TelemetryId` newtype with a smart constructor that validates non-empty and format constraints, returning a typed error.

findings.problem: The struct has only public fields with no smart constructor, no private fields, and no validation. Raw strings and booleans roam through the entire type without being parsed or validated at any boundary.
findings.failure_mode: Any caller can construct an instance in an illegal state; there is no parse boundary that converts external input into trusted domain data.
findings.fix: Make all fields private, provide a smart constructor that validates inputs and returns a typed error, and expose behavior through methods or a typestate API.

findings.problem: mark_sent takes ownership of the struct and mutates it in place with string assignment and boolean flip. There is no state guard: it can be called on an item that was never validated, and it sets status via raw string instead of enum variant.
findings.failure_mode: Unvalidated telemetry can be marked sent without any gate; the function hardcodes "sent" as a string literal, compounding the status-string violation; callers have no compile-time way to prevent calling mark_sent at the wrong lifecycle point.
findings.fix: Replace with a state-machine method or constructor that requires the validated state as input: e.g., `fn validate(item: Telemetry) -> Result<Telemetry, ValidationError>` and `fn send(item: ValidatedTelemetry) -> Result<SentTelemetry, SendError>`.

findings.problem: mark_sent allocates a new String via `.to_string()` on every call. There is no allocation budget, no benchmark, no profiler, and no second-ring allocation evidence.
findings.failure_mode: Hot-path allocation on every telemetry send increases GC pressure and latency; without benchmarks there is no measured baseline to optimize against.
findings.fix: Benchmark the allocation path; consider storing a &'static str enum discriminant instead of heap-allocating; add a second-ring allocation audit.

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for mark_sent allocation cost
no profiler evidence for hot-path analysis
no allocation audit or second-ring allocation tracking
no command-truth evidence (no build/test commands verified)
residual_risk: Static review only. The struct model permits invalid state combinations (sent without validated, timestamp without sent) that the compiler cannot prevent. Without typestate enums and smart constructors, runtime invariant checks are the only safeguard. No commands were run; build, test, clippy, and benchmark gates are unverified.
